mainTopic: Items that may or may not be moved on שבת: the משנה's list, the 'animal food' principle, כל ישראל בני מלכים, herb bundles, and salted versus unsalted meat
overview: The גמרא goes through the משנה's list of things that may not be moved on שבת. For טבל, מעשר ראשון, מעשר שני and הקדש, it asks 'פשיטא' and answers that the משנה means a borderline case: rabbinic טבל, a tithe the לוי took early from the pile, and invalid redemptions. On the לוף, a ברייתא permits moving animal food, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל even permits broken glass as food for ostriches. רבי נתן challenges this from elephants, and רב אשי rejects אמימר's limit, concluding that what counts is whether the item is suitable as food. אביי then shows that four תנאים hold כל ישראל בני מלכים הם. The גמרא next explains the משנה about bundles of straw and herbs, how herbs may be picked and crushed on שבת, and what the herb names mean. Finally, רב הונא and רב חסדא argue about moving unsalted meat, and a ברייתא allows moving meat and bones, which are food for dogs.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that טבל may not be moved?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that טבל may not be moved on שבת and asks why it needed to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'But not untithed produce, etc.' This is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that you may not move טבל on שבת. It asks why the משנה needed to say something so obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טבל is forbidden to eat, and on שבת you cannot take תרומות ומעשרות to fix it. So it is plainly useless on שבת and is מוקצה. The question 'פשיטא' pushes the גמרא to find a case where the rule is not obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which תרומות ומעשרות have not yet been taken; forbidden to eat
'It is obvious!' — asking why a rule needed to be stated
'Etc.' — the quote from the משנה continues

steps.confusionAlert: 'פשיטא' does not mean the גמרא disagrees with the משנה. It only asks why the משנה bothered to say it. The answer will show a case that is not obvious.

phrases.english: [The Mishnah said:] But not the untithed produce, etc.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: This is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens analysis of the משנה's list of items forbidden to move
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to state that טבל may not be moved
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: טבל cannot be eaten or fixed on שבת, so obviously it is מוקצה. Stating it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The משנה means produce that is טבל only by rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed for produce grown in a pot with no hole, which is טבל only מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only needed for produce that is טבל by rabbinic law, such as when one planted it in a flowerpot that has no hole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a less obvious case: produce that is טבל only מדרבנן. That happens when it grew in a pot without a hole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, produce grown in an עציץ שאינו נקוב is not considered 'from the ground,' so it is not obligated in מעשרות. The רבנן still made it טבל. We might have thought a merely rabbinic טבל could be moved, so the משנה teaches that it is מוקצה too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is only needed for…' — introduces the specific case the source means
Considered טבל only by rabbinic law
A flowerpot with no hole; what grows in it is not considered growing from the ground

phrases.english: It is only necessary
regarding untithed produce that is untithed by rabbinic law,
where he planted it in an unperforated flowerpot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא by narrowing the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Produce that is טבל only מדרבנן might be allowed to move on שבת
steps.terutzMaskana: Even rabbinic טבל is מוקצה and may not be moved

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that untithed מעשר ראשון may not be moved?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was not taken and asks why this needed to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Nor first tithe, etc.' This is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה: מעשר ראשון from which תרומה was not removed. It again asks why this needed to be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר ראשון that still has תרומה inside it is forbidden to eat, just like טבל. So it should obviously be מוקצה. The גמרא will again look for a less obvious case.

keyTerms.meaning: The first tithe, given to the לוי; he must separate תרומת מעשר from it

phrases.english: [The Mishnah said:] Nor first tithe, etc.
This is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 1, now applied to the next item in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to state that untithed מעשר ראשון may not be moved
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Untithed מעשר ראשון is forbidden to eat like טבל, so its status as מוקצה is obvious.

steps.title: The case where the לוי took his tithe from the pile early
steps.stepSummary: The משנה refers to the case where the לוי took מעשר ראשון from the pile before תרומה גדולה was taken.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only needed where he took it early from the pile: he took tithe from it, but the great תרומה had not been taken from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a special case. The לוי took his מעשר ראשון from a grain pile (כרי) before the כהן's תרומה גדולה was separated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally תרומה גדולה (about 1/50) is taken first, and only then מעשר ראשון. Here the לוי went first, so his tithe still contains the share of תרומה גדולה that belongs to the כהן. The question is whether this tithe is still obligated, and so still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: He did it first — the לוי took his portion before the כהן's portion
A pile of threshed and smoothed grain
The main תרומה given to the כהן, separated before the tithes

phrases.english: It is only necessary where he preceded [the priest] at the pile,
that he took the tithe from it
and the great teruma was not taken from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא by narrowing the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A tithe taken early might be exempt from תרומה גדולה and therefore allowed
steps.terutzMaskana: The tithe still owes תרומה גדולה and is forbidden

steps.title: Why this case is not obvious: the רב פפא and אביי exchange
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought, as רב פפא suggested, that the tithe is exempt. The משנה teaches as אביי answered, that it is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said as רב פפא said to אביי; it teaches us as אביי answered him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why this case needed teaching. It points to a known exchange between רב פפא and אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an exemption when the לוי takes his tithe while the grain is still on the stalks (שבלים). רב פפא asked why the same exemption should not apply in the pile. אביי answered that once the grain is in a pile it is already called 'דגן' and is obligated in תרומה. The משנה follows אביי: this tithe still owes תרומה, so it is מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might have said…' — introduces the mistaken assumption
'It teaches us…' — the new point the source adds

steps.whatToRemember: Each 'פשיטא' in this section is answered by finding a borderline case: rabbinic טבל, and a tithe taken early from the pile.

phrases.english: Lest you say
as Rav Pappa said to Abaye,
phrases.notes: That the pile case should be exempt just like the stalks case

phrases.english: it teaches us
as Abaye answered him.
phrases.notes: In a pile the grain is already 'דגן' and obligated

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְתֵימָא כְּדַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the case in step 4 is not obvious
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the mistaken assumption the משנה rules out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רב פפא, the tithe taken early in the pile is exempt
steps.terutzMaskana: Following אביי, it is obligated in תרומה גדולה and therefore forbidden

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that unredeemed מעשר שני may not be moved?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about unredeemed מעשר שני and הקדש and asks why this needed to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Nor second tithe, etc.' This is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next item: מעשר שני and הקדש that were not redeemed. It asks why this needed to be stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unredeemed מעשר שני cannot be eaten outside ירושלים. הקדש belongs to the Temple. Both are clearly unusable, so it seems obvious they are מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money

phrases.english: [The Mishnah said:] Nor second tithe, etc.
This is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same פשיטא pattern applied to the next item
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to forbid moving unredeemed מעשר שני and הקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unredeemed sanctified items are clearly forbidden for use, so they are obviously מוקצה.

steps.title: They were redeemed, but not properly
steps.stepSummary: The משנה refers to items that went through a redemption, but one that was not done according to הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only needed where they were redeemed, but not redeemed according to their law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה means items that someone tried to redeem, but in an invalid way. The next two steps explain each case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think any act of redemption is enough to free the item and make it usable. The משנה teaches that a flawed redemption does not work. So the items are still sanctified and מוקצה.

phrases.english: It is only necessary
where they were redeemed but not redeemed according to their law.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא דְּנִפְדּוּ וְלֹא נִפְדּוּ כְּהִלְכָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא by narrowing the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any redemption, even a flawed one, makes the item usable
steps.terutzMaskana: An invalid redemption does not work; the item stays forbidden

steps.title: מעשר שני redeemed with an unstamped coin
steps.stepSummary: For מעשר שני, the improper redemption is with an אסימון, metal with no stamped image, while the פסוק requires money with a form.
steps.simpleTranslation: Second tithe: where he redeemed it with an unminted coin, because the Torah says 'And you shall bind up the money in your hand,' meaning something that has a form on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the flawed redemption for מעשר שני. Someone used an אסימון, a blank piece of metal with no picture or stamp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'וצרת הכסף.' The word וצרת is read as related to צורה, a form or image. So מעשר שני must be redeemed with a stamped coin, and an אסימון does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: An unstamped coin or blank piece of metal
'And you shall bind up the money' (דברים יד:כה)
A form or image stamped on a coin

phrases.english: Tithe — where he redeemed it with an unminted coin,
for the Torah said:
'And you shall bind up the money in your hand,'
[meaning] something that has a form on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case with a source from a פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: Redeeming מעשר שני with an אסימון is invalid

steps.title: הקדש redeemed with land instead of money
steps.stepSummary: For הקדש, the improper redemption is with land, while the פסוק requires money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Consecrated property: where he redeemed it with land, because the Torah says 'He shall give the money and it shall be his.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the flawed redemption for הקדש. Someone exchanged it for land instead of money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'ונתן הכסף וקם לו,' which ties the redemption of הקדש to money. Land is not money, so the redemption fails. The item stays הקדש and מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: He redeemed it (removed its holiness onto something else)
'He shall give the money and it shall be his' (ויקרא כז:יט)

steps.whatToRemember: The obvious-seeming items are taught for borderline cases: rabbinic טבל, a tithe taken early from the pile, and invalid redemptions (אסימון for מעשר שני, land for הקדש).

phrases.english: Consecrated property — where he redeemed it with land,
for the Torah said:
'And he shall give the money and it shall be assured to him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case with a source from a פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: Redeeming הקדש with land is invalid

steps.title: A ברייתא: squill and mustard may be moved because animals eat them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reaches the לוף and quotes a ברייתא allowing one to move חצב (food for deer) and חרדל (food for doves).
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] 'Nor arum.' The Rabbis taught: One may move squill because it is food for deer, and mustard because it is food for doves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's item 'not the לוף' and brings a ברייתא about plants that may be moved because animals eat them. This sets up the next steps, which continue the ברייתא with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling on broken glass and רבי נתן's challenge to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's principle is that something which serves as food for animals is not מוקצה. This is the same reasoning רבן שמעון בן גמליאל uses in the משנה to permit the לוף, because ravens eat it. The גמרא brings the ברייתא to develop this 'animal food' principle and to find its limits.

keyTerms.meaning: Arum, a plant with an edible root
Squill, a plant with deep roots

phrases.english: [The Mishnah said:] Nor the arum.
The Rabbis taught:
One may move squill
because it is food for deer,
and mustard
because it is food for doves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the משנה and brings an outside source
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything that is food for animals, such as חצב for deer and חרדל for doves, may be moved on שבת

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: even broken glass, food for ostriches
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל extends the rule: even broken glass may be moved, because ostriches eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: One may even move shards of glass, because they are food for ostriches.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who goes further than the first opinion. He allows moving broken glass because ostriches eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This pushes the 'animal food' principle very far. Even something no person would ever eat, broken glass, counts as food if some animal eats it. This far-reaching claim is what רבי נתן challenges in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who here extends the rule

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
One may even move shards of glass
because they are food for ostriches.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אַף מְטַלְטְלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the ברייתא's rule to broken glass
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Broken glass may be moved on שבת because it is food for ostriches

steps.title: רבי נתן: Then Grapevines Should Be Movable for Elephants
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן challenges רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. If glass may be moved because ostriches eat it, then grapevine bundles should be movable because elephants eat them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן said to him: If so, bundles of grapevines should also be movable, because they are food for elephants!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן attacks רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule about broken glass. He argues that the same logic leads to a result nobody accepts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said an object counts as food if some animal eats it. רבי נתן pushes this to its extreme. Elephants eat grapevine bundles, so those bundles should be movable on שבת too, which sounds absurd.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, from now on (introduces an absurd result of someone's logic)

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan said to him:
If so, from now on
bundles of grapevines should be movable
because they are food for elephants!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the extension stated by רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule that broken glass is movable because ostriches eat it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum. If any animal's food counts, then grapevines (elephant food) would also be permitted.

steps.title: Ostriches Are Common, Elephants Are Not
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל answers that ostriches are commonly found while elephants are not. So only food for common animals counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבן שמעון בן גמליאל answers: ostriches are common, but elephants are not common.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל defends his ruling. He explains why glass and grapevines are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not 'any animal anywhere.' An item counts as food only if it feeds an animal people commonly keep or find. Ostriches qualify and elephants do not, so the grapevine case does not follow.

phrases.english: And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel (answers):
ostriches are common,
elephants are not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי נתן's challenge from step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the cases (common versus uncommon animal).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any animal's food makes an item movable, even food for a rare animal like an elephant.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only food for commonly found animals counts. Ostriches qualify; elephants do not.

steps.title: אמימר: Only If He Owns Ostriches
steps.stepSummary: אמימר limits רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling. Glass may be moved only by someone who actually has ostriches.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: And this applies only where he has ostriches.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר adds a condition to the ruling about broken glass.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אמימר, it is not enough that ostriches are common in the world. This particular person must own ostriches for the glass to count as his animal food.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is only when (introduces a limiting condition)

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
And that is only where he has ostriches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the scope of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Broken glass is movable only for someone who personally owns ostriches.

steps.title: רב אשי: רבי נתן's Question Shows Ownership Is Not the Test
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges אמימר using רבי נתן's question. If owning the animal were the test, someone who owns elephants could obviously move grapevines, so the question would make no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: But what about what רבי נתן said to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, that grapevine bundles should be movable because they are food for elephants? If he has elephants, why not?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי argues against אמימר's condition. He uses the earlier exchange between רבי נתן and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל as evidence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule depended on owning the animal, then someone who owns elephants could obviously move grapevines. רבי נתן's challenge would then be pointless. His question only makes sense if the discussion is about the item in general, regardless of who owns which animal.

keyTerms.meaning: רב אשי, a leading later אמורא

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
But that which Rabbi Natan said
to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel:
'one should be able to move bundles of grapevines
because they are food for elephants'

phrases.aramaic: אִי אִית לֵיהּ פִּילִין — אַמַּאי לָא?
phrases.english: if he has elephants, why not?
phrases.notes: If he owned elephants, moving their food would obviously be allowed, so רבי נתן could not have meant that case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אמימר's limitation from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's condition that the person must own ostriches.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי נתן's challenge assumes ownership is irrelevant. Otherwise, an elephant owner could obviously move grapevines and there would be nothing to ask.

steps.title: The Test Is Whether It Is Suitable
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי concludes that the test is whether the item is suitable as animal food. Broken glass is suitable for ostriches, so it is movable even for someone without ostriches.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the issue is whether it is suitable; here too, the issue is whether it is suitable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his argument and states the correct standard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether an item is movable depends on its general fitness as food for a common animal. It does not depend on what this person happens to own. So the glass is movable for everyone, which overturns אמימר's limit.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, an item counts as animal food on שבת if it is suitable for a common animal. It does not matter whether this person owns that animal.

phrases.english: Rather, (the criterion is) suitable,
here too, (the criterion is) suitable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion of רב אשי's challenge.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Broken glass is movable because it is suitable food for ostriches, even for someone who owns none.

steps.title: אביי: Four תנאים Hold That All Jews Are Princes
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, רבי שמעון, רבי ישמעאל, and רבי עקיבא all hold the principle כל ישראל בני מלכים הם.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, רבי שמעון, רבי ישמעאל, and רבי עקיבא all hold that all Jews are children of kings.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי states a general principle shared by four תנאים. He is setting up a series of proofs, one for each of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling every Jew a prince means we judge what is usable or fitting by the standard of royalty. Something that seems luxurious or far-fetched for an ordinary person is still treated as fitting for any Jew. This explains why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל treats glass as ostrich food for everyone, as if everyone keeps exotic animals like a king would.

keyTerms.meaning: All Jews are children of kings (princes)

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle appears in several halachic areas. It treats every Jew as entitled to the standards of royalty when defining what is usable or fitting.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and Rabbi Shimon
and Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva
all of them hold
all Jews are children of kings.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלְּהוּ סְבִירָא לְהוּ כׇּל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּנֵי מְלָכִים הֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the specific ruling to name the broader principle behind it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four תנאים share the view that every Jew has the status of a prince.

steps.title: Proof for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: What We Just Said
steps.stepSummary: The proof that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds this principle is the ruling already discussed. He treats animal food as usable for every Jew, as if every Jew keeps such animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: that which we said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins proving אביי's list, starting with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. It points back to his ruling discussed above.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits moving the לוף because it is food for ravens, and in the ברייתא he permits broken glass as food for ostriches. Treating such items as usable for everyone assumes every Jew might keep these animals, as a prince would. The next two steps prove the other three names on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: That which we said (pointing back to an earlier discussion)

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel:
that which we said.
phrases.notes: Points back to his ruling on moving animal food (broken glass for ostriches). Sefaria's translation connects it to the לוף being food for ravens.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins proving אביי's claim, starting with the first name on his list.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds כל ישראל בני מלכים הם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: His ruling permitting the moving of items that serve as animal food (לוף for ravens in the משנה; broken glass for ostriches in the ברייתא).

steps.title: Proof that רבי שמעון holds every Jew is royalty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves רבי שמעון holds כל ישראל בני מלכים הם from a משנה about princes putting rose oil on wounds on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we see רבי שמעון holds this? As we learned in a משנה: princes may put rose oil on their wounds on שבת, because princes normally rub themselves with it on weekdays. רבי שמעון says: all Jews are princes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues proving אביי's list. Now it shows that רבי שמעון holds every Jew is treated like a prince.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Healing a wound on שבת is normally a problem. But if a person normally uses rose oil on a weekday even without a wound, putting it on does not look like healing. The first opinion allows this only for real princes. רבי שמעון says every Jew counts as a prince, so every Jew may do it.

keyTerms.meaning: They smear or rub on oil
Rose oil, an expensive scented oil

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon — as we learned in a Mishnah:
phrases.notes: Introduces the proof for the second name on אביי's list.

phrases.aramaic: בְּנֵי מְלָכִים סָכִין עַל גַּבֵּי מַכּוֹתֵיהֶן
phrases.english: Princes may smear on their wounds
phrases.notes: On שבת.

phrases.english: rose oil,
since it is the way of princes
phrases.notes: This is the reason. It is their normal habit, so it does not look like medicine.

phrases.english: to smear it on during the week.
Rabbi Shimon says:
All Jews are princes.
phrases.notes: So every Jew may use rose oil this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of proofs for אביי's statement. Step 18 proved רבן שמעון בן גמליאל; this step proves רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds כל ישראל בני מלכים הם
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about princes smearing rose oil on wounds on שבת

steps.title: Proof that רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא hold every Jew is royalty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא hold the principle from a ברייתא about a debtor who wears a very expensive cloak.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we see רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא hold this? As a ברייתא teaches: if creditors demand a debt of a thousand מנה from a man, and he is wearing a cloak worth a hundred מנה, they take that cloak off him and dress him in a cloak fit for him. It was taught in the name of רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא: every Jew is fit for that cloak.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the last proof for אביי's list. It shows that רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא also treat every Jew like royalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a creditor may not take the clothes a debtor needs. The first opinion says a super-expensive cloak is too fancy for this debtor, so it can be sold and swapped for a simpler one. רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא say every Jew deserves such a cloak. So it counts as his normal clothing and is not taken from him.

keyTerms.meaning: Creditors are demanding money from him
A unit of money (one hundred דינר)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's four תנאים all share one idea: הלכה treats every Jew like royalty. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל applies it to animal food, רבי שמעון to rose oil, and רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא to a royal cloak.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva — as was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיוּ נוֹשִׁין בּוֹ אֶלֶף מָנֶה
phrases.english: One from whom creditors were demanding a thousand maneh
phrases.notes: Sefaria reads it as a thousand times one hundred.

phrases.english: and he was wearing a cloak worth a hundred maneh —
they strip it off him,
phrases.notes: And sell it to pay the debt.

phrases.english: and dress him in a cloak fit for him.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וּמִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Yishmael and in the name of Rabbi Akiva:
All Jews are fit for that cloak.
phrases.notes: So it is not taken from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final proof in אביי's list, after רבי שמעון in Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא hold כל ישראל בני מלכים הם
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a debtor wearing a cloak worth a hundred מנה

steps.title: Bundles prepared for animal food may be moved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה about bundles and quotes a ברייתא: bundles of straw, wood, or twigs prepared for animal food may be moved on שבת, otherwise not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Bundles of straw and bundles of...' The רבנן taught: bundles of straw, bundles of wood, and bundles of twigs, if he prepared them for animal food, he may move them. If not, he may not move them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the next line of the משנה, about bundles. It quotes a ברייתא that gives the basic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Straw, wood, and twigs are not usually used on שבת, so they would be מוקצה. If the owner set them aside before שבת as animal food, they gain a use and may be moved. Without that preparation, they stay מוקצה.

phrases.english: Bundles of straw and bundles of, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, marking the new topic.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: חֲבִילֵי קַשׁ וַחֲבִילֵי עֵצִים וַחֲבִילֵי זְרָדִים,
phrases.english: Bundles of straw, bundles of wood, and bundles of twigs,
if he prepared them for animal food —
phrases.notes: Before שבת.

phrases.english: one may move them,
and if not — one may not move them.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲבִילֵי קַשׁ וַחֲבִילֵי כּוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the כל ישראל בני מלכים discussion and returns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bundles of straw, wood, or twigs prepared for animal food may be moved on שבת; otherwise they may not.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's size test for bundles
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says bundles that can be lifted with one hand may be moved, but bundles that need two hands may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: bundles that are picked up with one hand may be moved. Bundles that need two hands may not be moved.
steps.whatsHappening: In the same ברייתא, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives a different test for bundles, based on their size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion looked at whether the bundles were prepared for animal food. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל uses weight instead. A small bundle is easy to carry, so moving it is allowed. A big bundle that needs two hands means heavy work, so moving it is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Bundles that are picked up with one hand —
it is permitted to move them,
phrases.notes: No great effort is involved.

phrases.english: with two hands — it is forbidden to move them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second opinion in the same ברייתא, using size instead of preparation as the test.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bundles lifted with one hand may be moved on שבת; bundles that need two hands may not.

steps.title: Herb bundles depend on why they were brought in
steps.stepSummary: Bundles of fragrant herbs brought in for firewood may not be used on שבת, but if brought in for animal food, one may take from them on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bundles of savory, hyssop, and thyme: if he brought them in to use as firewood, he may not take from them on שבת. If he brought them in for animal food, he may take from them on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with herb bundles. The rule depends on what the owner planned to use them for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These herbs can be eaten by people, but they can also be burned. If the owner brought them in as firewood, he set them aside for burning, which is not allowed on שבת, so they are מוקצה. If he brought them in as animal food, they were set aside for a use that is allowed on שבת, so he may take from them.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes from them for his needs

steps.confusionAlert: These herbs are fit for people to eat, yet they can still be forbidden. What decides it is the owner's plan when he brought them in, not the herb itself.

phrases.english: Bundles of savory, hyssop, and thyme,
if he brought them in for firewood —
he may not take from them on Shabbat,
for animal food — he may take from them on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with a new case: herb bundles whose status depends on the owner's plan.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Herb bundles brought in as firewood are מוקצה on שבת; herb bundles brought in as animal food may be used.

steps.title: How one may pick and crush herbs to eat on Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. One may pinch off herbs by hand and eat them, but not with a tool. רבי יהודה lets one crush them, as long as one does not crush a lot with a tool. חכמים allow crushing only with the fingertips, not with the whole hand the way one does on a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may pinch off the herbs by hand and eat, as long as he does not pinch them off with a tool. And one may crush them and eat, as long as he does not crush a lot with a tool. These are the words of רבי יהודה. חכמים say: he may crush with his fingertips and eat, as long as he does not crush a lot with his hand the way he does on a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step keeps going. It explains how you may take herbs from an animal-food bundle and get them ready to eat on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions allow eating the herbs, but both want the preparation to look different from weekday work. רבי יהודה forbids only using a tool to crush a large amount. חכמים are stricter: you may not even use your whole hand, only your fingertips, which is an unusual way of doing it.

keyTerms.meaning: pinches off or picks off leaves
crushes or rubs the herb between the fingers
the way he does it on a weekday

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree you may crush the herbs. The argument is only about how you may do it: רבי יהודה forbids only a tool, while חכמים also forbid the normal full-hand method.

phrases.english: And he may pinch off by hand and eat,
as long as he does not pinch off with a tool.
And he may crush and eat,
as long as he does not crush a lot with a tool,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
And the Sages say:
He may crush with the tips of his fingers and eat,
as long as he does not crush a lot with his hand
the way he does on a weekday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא about herb bundles brought in for animal food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may pinch off herbs by hand, but not with a tool. On crushing, רבי יהודה forbids only crushing a lot with a tool. חכמים allow fingertips only and forbid crushing a lot with the hand in the weekday manner.

steps.title: The same rule applies to other spices
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that the same rules apply to אמיתא, to פיגם (rue), and to all other spices.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same is true for אמיתא, for פיגם, and for all other kinds of spices.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by stretching the same rules to other herbs and spices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules about picking and crushing are not limited to the herbs named earlier. Any spice plant follows the same pattern. The unfamiliar word אמיתא also sets up the גמרא's next question.

keyTerms.meaning: a kind of herb (explained in the next step as mint)

phrases.english: And the same with amita, and the same with rue,
and the same with all other kinds of spices.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule of the previous step to more spices.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The picking and crushing rules apply to all spices.

steps.title: What is אמיתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what אמיתא is and answers that it is mint (נינייא).
steps.simpleTranslation: What is אמיתא? It is נינייא, mint.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to explain an unfamiliar plant name from the ברייתא. It asks and answers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a challenge. It is a simple word-definition question. It gives the Hebrew name אמיתא its everyday Aramaic name, so we know which plant the law means.

phrases.english: What is amita? Mint.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines a word from the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which plant the word אמיתא refers to.

steps.title: רב יהודה identifies סיאה, אזוב, and קורנית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about סיאה, the herb from the earlier list. רב יהודה says סיאה is צתרי (savory) and אזוב is אברתא (hyssop). About קורנית, he says it has no other name; it is simply called קורניתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is סיאה? רב יהודה said: סיאה is צתרי. אזוב is אברתא. קורנית is just called קורניתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps defining plant names, this time the herbs listed earlier in the ברייתא about bundles. רב יהודה gives the everyday name of each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For two herbs רב יהודה gives a familiar Aramaic name. For קורנית he says there is no other known name. That last claim is what the גמרא will challenge next.

phrases.english: What is sia?
Rav Yehuda said: (Sia is) savory.
Ezov is hyssop (avrata).
Koranit — its name is simply koranita.
phrases.notes: Meaning: there is no other everyday name for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the word definitions, moving to the herbs in the earlier part of the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סיאה is savory, אזוב is hyssop, and קורנית has no other name.

steps.title: The seller of קורניתא was selling thyme
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's claim that קורנית has no other name. A seller once called out, 'Who wants קורניתא?', and it turned out he was selling חשי (thyme).
steps.simpleTranslation: But there was that man who said to people, 'Who wants קורניתא?', and it turned out he was selling חשי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last part of רב יהודה's statement by telling a real-life story about a seller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said קורנית has no other name. But the seller used the word קורניתא for something people knew as חשי. So קורנית does have a familiar name: thyme.

keyTerms.meaning: but look, here is a problem
it was found, it turned out

phrases.english: But there was that one who said to them:
Who wants koranita?
And it turned out to be thyme!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim in the previous step that קורנית has no other name.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's statement that קורנית is known only as קורניתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real seller used קורניתא for חשי, which shows the plant is known by a familiar name.

steps.title: Corrected list: קורניתא is thyme
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the identification list: סיאה is savory, אזוב is hyssop, and קורניתא is חשי (thyme).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it this way: סיאה is צתרי, אזוב is אברתא, and קורניתא is חשי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and restates the list with a correction for קורנית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two identifications stay the same. Only קורנית changes: it is no longer a plant with no other name, but thyme. The word אלא tells us the earlier version is being replaced.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, here is the corrected version

steps.whatToRemember: Final identifications: אמיתא is mint, סיאה is savory, אזוב is hyssop, and קורנית is thyme.

phrases.english: Rather: sia is savory,
ezov is hyssop,
koranita is thyme.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by correcting the identification of קורנית.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קורנית has no other everyday name.

steps.title: Moving salted and unsalted meat on Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: A new teaching: salted meat may be moved on שבת. About unsalted meat, רב הונא says it may be moved, and רב חסדא says it may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: salted meat may be moved on שבת. Unsalted meat: רב הונא says it may be moved, and רב חסדא says it may not be moved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic about which foods count as usable, and so may be moved, on שבת. It opens with a disagreement between אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salted meat is ready to eat, so everyone agrees it may be moved. Unsalted, raw meat is less clearly usable, so רב הונא and רב חסדא argue over whether it counts as מוקצה. The גמרא will explain their reasoning next.

keyTerms.meaning: it was stated (introduces a teaching of the אמוראים)

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new discussion about which foods count as מוקצה, a question that matters for הלכה למעשה.

phrases.english: It was stated:
Salted meat may be moved on Shabbat.
Unsalted meat:
Rav Huna said: it may be moved;
Rav Ḥisda said: it may not be moved.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: בָּשָׂר מָלִיחַ מוּתָּר לְטַלְטְלוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the herb discussion and starts a new topic about moving food on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salted meat may be moved on שבת. For unsalted meat, רב הונא permits moving it and רב חסדא forbids it.

steps.title: How can רב הונא permit moving unsalted meat if his teacher holds of מוקצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא. He is a student of רב, and רב follows רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה. So how can רב הונא permit moving unsalted meat?
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב הונא really say it is permitted to move it? But רב הונא was a student of רב, and רב holds like רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's ruling from Step 30. It says his view seems to clash with the view of his own teacher, רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unsalted meat is not ready to eat on שבת, so it could count as מוקצה. רבי יהודה holds that such things are מוקצה, and רב usually follows רבי יהודה. A student would not normally argue with his teacher, so רב הונא's permission to move the meat looks like a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Something 'set aside' that may not be used or moved on שבת

phrases.english: Did Rav Huna say it is permitted to move it?
phrases.notes: Quoting Step 30 in order to question it

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַב הוּנָא תַּלְמִיד דְּרַב הֲוָה
phrases.english: But wasn't Rav Huna a student of Rav?
And Rav holds like Rabbi Yehuda
who holds of muktzeh?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַב הוּנָא תַּלְמִיד דְּרַב הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling from Step 30
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that unsalted meat may be moved
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב הונא's teacher רב follows רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה. So רב הונא should forbid moving unsalted meat.

steps.title: רב splits the two laws: eating follows רבי יהודה, moving follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב follows רבי יהודה only about eating מוקצה food. About moving it, רב follows רבי שמעון. So רב הונא's permission to move the meat fits his teacher's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: For מוקצה regarding eating, he holds like רבי יהודה. For מוקצה regarding moving, he holds like רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא. It shows that רב himself does not apply רבי יהודה's view to moving things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that רב follows רבי יהודה in every area of מוקצה. The answer splits מוקצה into two areas: eating and moving. רב is strict like רבי יהודה about eating, but lenient like רבי שמעון about moving. So רב הונא is following his teacher after all.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume a sage follows one opinion in every case. Here רב follows רבי יהודה for eating but רבי שמעון for moving.
steps.whyThisMatters: This split between eating and moving is a key tool for understanding רב's approach to מוקצה.

phrases.english: With regard to muktzeh for eating
he holds like Rabbi Yehuda
with regard to muktzeh for moving
he holds like Rabbi Shimon

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 31
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between two areas of the same law (eating vs. moving)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב follows רבי יהודה in every area of מוקצה, so moving should be forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: רב follows רבי יהודה only for eating; for moving he follows רבי שמעון, so רב הונא can permit moving

steps.title: Story challenges רב חסדא: his household moved a duck out of the sun
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's ruling that unsalted meat may not be moved. רב יצחק בר אמי visited רב חסדא's house and saw them moving a duck from the sun to the shade, and רב חסדא said there was a money loss to worry about.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said it is forbidden to move it. But רב יצחק בר אמי once came to רב חסדא's house. He saw a duck being moved from the sun to the shade, and רב חסדא said: 'We see a monetary loss here!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to רב חסדא's side. It brings a story that seems to show רב חסדא allowed moving unsalted meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא forbids moving unsalted meat. Yet in his own home they moved an unsalted duck so it would not spoil, and he approved, citing the money loss. This looks like he permits moving unsalted meat after all.

keyTerms.meaning: From the sun to the shade

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said it is forbidden to move it
phrases.notes: Quoting Step 30 as the target

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yitzchak bar Ami
happen to come to Rav Chisda's house
and he saw that duck
that they were moving it
from the sun to the shade
and Rav Chisda said
We see a monetary loss here!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַמֵּי אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from defending רב הונא to challenging רב חסדא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that unsalted meat may not be moved
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In רב חסדא's own house they moved an unsalted duck, and he approved because of the money loss. So he seems to permit moving unsalted meat.

steps.title: A duck is different because it can be eaten raw
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a duck is a special case. Its meat is fit to be eaten raw, so it is not מוקצה even when unsalted.
steps.simpleTranslation: A duck is different, because it is fit to be eaten as raw meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא. It explains that the duck in the story was an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא forbids moving unsalted meat because it is not ready to eat. Duck meat, however, can be eaten raw, so it is usable and may be moved. The story therefore does not contradict his general rule.

phrases.english: A duck is different
since it is fit to be eaten as raw meat

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 33
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The duck story shows רב חסדא permits moving all unsalted meat
steps.terutzMaskana: Duck meat is edible raw, so it is an exception; other unsalted meat stays forbidden to move according to רב חסדא

steps.title: ברייתא: salted fish may be moved, unsalted fish may not, all meat may be moved
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that salted fish may be moved on שבת and unsalted fish may not. Meat, salted or unsalted, may be moved. This matches רב הונא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Salted fish may be moved. Unsalted fish may not be moved. Meat, whether unsalted or salted, may be moved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that speaks directly about moving fish and meat on שבת. Its ruling on meat supports רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats fish and meat differently. Unsalted fish is not usable, so it may not be moved. Meat may be moved even when unsalted, exactly as רב הונא ruled.

phrases.english: The Sages taught
Salted fish: it is permitted to move it
Unsalted fish: it is forbidden to move it
Meat, whether unsalted or salted
it is permitted to move it

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן דָּג מָלִיחַ מוּתָּר לְטַלְטְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on the same question as the מחלוקת in Step 30
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling that unsalted meat may be moved
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that permits moving meat whether salted or unsalted

steps.title: The unattributed ברייתא follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this anonymous ברייתא follows the view of רבי שמעון, who is lenient about מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this unattributed ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא labels whose view the ברייתא follows. It is רבי שמעון's lenient approach to מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Permitting unsalted meat to be moved fits רבי שמעון, who does not hold of this kind of מוקצה. This ties back to Step 32, where רב follows רבי שמעון regarding moving.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who is lenient about מוקצה

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא permits moving unsalted meat because רב follows רבי שמעון for moving, even though he follows רבי יהודה for eating. רב חסדא forbids it, and the duck story is an exception because duck can be eaten raw. The ברייתא permitting all meat to be moved follows רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: And the unattributed teaching follows Rabbi Shimon

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies whose opinion the ברייתא of Step 35 follows
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא permitting the moving of all meat follows רבי שמעון's lenient view on מוקצה

steps.title: Bones may be moved because they are dog food
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that bones may be moved on שבת, because they are food for dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught in a ברייתא: You may move bones on שבת, because they are food for dogs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new ברייתא. It rules that bones may be moved on שבת because dogs can eat them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People do not eat bones, so you might think bones are מוקצה and may not be moved. The ברייתא says they still have a real use, because they can feed dogs. Food that is fit for animals counts as usable, so it may be moved on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Rabbis taught": the standard way to open a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: The reason is not that people eat bones. The reason is that dogs eat them. Having a use for animals is enough to allow moving them on שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This applies a general idea already seen with the חצב and the חרדל: an item does not have to be human food to be moved on שבת. If it is fit to feed animals, it has a use, and that use permits moving it.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
phrases.notes: Opens a ברייתא

phrases.english: One may move bones (on Shabbat)
because they are food for dogs.
phrases.notes: The reason: they have a use as animal food

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא about fish and meat (which follows רבי שמעון), the גמרא brings another ברייתא about moving food items on שבת. This one deals with things fit only for animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bones may be moved on שבת because they are fit as food for dogs, so they are not treated as useless.
